notes: CBSE does not publish its own Classes 1-5 mathematics syllabus; CBSE schools follow the NCERT textbooks. The 2026-27 prescription was confirmed via official government split-up syllabi (Delhi Directorate of Education; KVS where available) and the NCERT reprint 2026-27 label.

NCERT's 'Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage' (tilops101.pdf) could not be opened (robots-blocked); outcomes are written in my own words from the chapter content and the official DoE/KVS split-up outcomes.
Outcomes are not copied from the textbook; questionTypes and difficulty are my judgement.
Textbook is a single annual volume; CBSE has no term split for these books, so term is null. School split-ups (DoE Delhi) divide chapters across mid-term and annual exams, which varies by school.
All 15 chapter titles verified on NCERT's contents page (eemm1ps.pdf). Chapter 10 contents reads 'Symmetrical Designs' (the chapter opening page reads 'Symmetrical Design').
DoE Delhi 2026-27 split-up teaches chapters in a different order (We the Travellers II alongside I); the book's numbering is used here.

Section headings were read through the fetch tool's text extraction/summary, not by viewing the page. Recurring activity labels ('Let Us Do', 'Let Us Think', 'Let Us Find', 'Let Us Compare', 'Let Us Explore', 'Let Us Solve', 'Try This', 'Discuss', 'Note for Teachers', 'Did you know?') are omitted. In chapter 5, headings reported in the form 'Let Us Explore / Measuring Long Distances' are recorded by their topical part only.
Chapter 1: the extraction also reported 'Reading and writing large numbers' as the first section, but it looked like a summary rather than a printed heading, so it is omitted.
Chapter 3: an opening activity heading "Let us play 'Statue'" and a 'Try these' box are omitted.

Chapter 6 (The Dairy Farm) and Chapter 14 (Maps and Locations) PDFs were robots-blocked: sections [] and outcomes based on the DoE split-up (doubling/halving, nearest multiples, patterns; directions and map reading). The multi-digit multiplication outcome for chapter 6 is my inference.
Chapter 11: only three printed headings were reported ('Comparing Shapes', 'Let Us Explore', 'Let Us Play'); only 'Comparing Shapes' is topical.
Chapter 13 (Animal Jumps) has no printed section headings beyond the chapter title, so sections is [].
Chapter 15 PDF also contains the book's Learning Material Sheets; those are not sections.

outcomes.statement: Read and write five-digit numbers in figures and words using the Indian place-value system and commas.
Round numbers to the nearest ten, hundred and thousand using number lines.

proposed.name: Round numbers to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand
proposed.why: MATH.reasoning.estimate-check covers checking answers by estimation but not the rounding procedure itself.

outcomes.statement: Estimate large quantities met in real contexts such as travel distances.
Solve logic puzzles by systematic reasoning, such as crossing problems and winning strategies.

proposed.name: Reason systematically to solve puzzles and strategy games
proposed.why: Puzzles and two-player strategy games (e.g. NIM, magic triangles, river crossing) recur across books; no existing reasoning entry targets systematic search or winning-position analysis.

sections.title: Comparing Fractions With Reference to 1 (a whole)

outcomes.statement: Represent fractions on grids and recognise that the same fraction can look different in different wholes.
Generate equivalent fractions by splitting parts further, noticing that numerator and denominator are multiplied by the same number.
Compare fractions with the same denominator or the same numerator.
Write fractions greater than 1 as improper fractions and mixed numbers and place them on a number line.

proposed.name: Convert between mixed and improper fractions
proposed.why: No existing entry covers improper fractions and mixed numbers (same id as cbse-g06).

outcomes.statement: Compare fractions by relating each to one-half or to one whole.
Describe a turn as a fraction of a full turn (quarter, half, three-quarter) and link it to the angle formed.

proposed.name: Describe angles as fractions of a turn and direction of turning
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.angles-intro compares angle types statically; angle as an amount of turning (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 turn, clockwise/anticlockwise) is a distinct skill.

outcomes.statement: Classify angles as right, acute, obtuse or straight.
Make and use a paper angle tool divided into equal parts to measure turns in eighths.
Describe clockwise and anticlockwise turns and the compass direction faced after a turn.

proposed.name: Describe angles as fractions of a turn and direction of turning
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.angles-intro compares angle types statically; angle as an amount of turning (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 turn, clockwise/anticlockwise) is a distinct skill.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

sections.title: The Longest Land Route — Adding Large Numbers

outcomes.statement: Add and subtract numbers up to five digits with regrouping, aligning place values.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Use the relationship between addition and subtraction to write related facts and check answers.
Use mental shortcuts such as complements to 100, 1000 and 10000 and subtracting 9 or 99.

proposed.name: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping
proposed.why: Existing regrouping entries are for two-digit numbers (Grade 2); there is no entry for 3- to 5-digit column or strategy-based addition/subtraction.

outcomes.statement: Investigate sums of consecutive numbers and the parity of sums of even and odd numbers.

proposed.name: Classify numbers as even or odd
proposed.why: Parity (pairing, even/odd sums) is assessed from Grade 4 onward and has no existing entry.

outcomes.statement: Solve multi-step word problems using data from tables, such as heights of mountain peaks.
Choose a suitable unit (mm, cm, m or km) for a given length or distance.
Convert among millimetres, centimetres, metres and kilometres.
Measure objects to the nearest millimetre and draw segments of given lengths.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide lengths given in mixed units.

proposed.name: Calculate with measured quantities in mixed units
proposed.why: Conversion entries exist, but adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths, weights and capacities given in mixed units (e.g. 2 kg 300 g) has no entry.

outcomes.statement: Estimate heights and distances using known reference lengths and relate feet and inches to centimetres.
Use doubling, halving and nearest multiples to work out products.
Multiply multi-digit numbers using place value and partial products.
Spot and explain patterns in multiplication facts.
Solve multiplication word problems in farm contexts.
Describe and extend repeating weaving patterns as ordered sequences.
Decide which regular polygons tessellate by checking whether their angles fit around a point.
Identify squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms and kites from descriptions of sides and angles.

proposed.name: Classify quadrilaterals by side, angle and diagonal properties
proposed.why: Same id as used in cbse-g08 (Grade 8 adds diagonal properties). MATH.geometry.quadrilaterals is about angle-sum properties; naming square/rectangle/rhombus/parallelogram/kite from side and angle properties has no entry.

outcomes.statement: Make shapes from tangram pieces and describe the pieces' sides and angles.
Match nets and views of cubes, count faces, edges and vertices of polyhedra, and count painted faces in cube stacks.

sections.title: Big to Small, Small to Big

outcomes.statement: Judge whether a recorded weight is sensible and choose between mg, g and kg.
Convert between kilograms, grams and milligrams and compare weights with <, = and >.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide weights in mixed units and find unit costs.

proposed.name: Calculate with measured quantities in mixed units
proposed.why: Conversion entries exist, but adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths, weights and capacities given in mixed units (e.g. 2 kg 300 g) has no entry.

outcomes.statement: Convert between litres and millilitres and calculate with capacities.

proposed.name: Calculate with measured quantities in mixed units
proposed.why: Conversion entries exist, but adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths, weights and capacities given in mixed units (e.g. 2 kg 300 g) has no entry.

sections.title: Patterns in Division and Place Value

outcomes.statement: Write division facts from a multiplication fact and use dividend = divisor x quotient.
Divide multiples of 10, 100 and 1000 using place-value patterns.

proposed.name: Multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000
proposed.why: No existing entry covers the place-value effect of multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 and 1000 and by their multiples.

outcomes.statement: Divide mentally by splitting the dividend or halving repeatedly.
Carry out long division with remainders and check using N = D x Q + R.
Decide whether statements about numbers and operations are always, sometimes or never true and justify.
Solve multi-step problems from a table of quantities and costs with missing values.

sections.title: Let Us Make a Windmill Firki

outcomes.statement: Find horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry in letters, digits and numbers.
Recognise rotational symmetry and the fraction of a turn after which a design looks the same.

proposed.name: Recognise rotational symmetry
proposed.why: Existing symmetry entries cover folding/line symmetry only.

outcomes.statement: Create symmetrical designs with paper cut-outs and block printing and describe their symmetry.

proposed.name: Recognise rotational symmetry
proposed.why: Existing symmetry entries cover folding/line symmetry only.

outcomes.statement: Compare areas by counting unit squares and estimate the area of irregular shapes.
Calculate the area and perimeter of rectangles and squares.
Show that shapes with equal area can have different perimeters and vice versa.

proposed.name: Compare shapes with equal area or equal perimeter
proposed.why: Area and perimeter entries compute each separately; recognising that equal area need not mean equal perimeter (and vice versa) is a distinct reasoning skill.

outcomes.statement: Solve word problems on area and perimeter of real objects.
Find the elapsed time between two clock times, including in 24-hour format.

proposed.name: Convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time
proposed.why: No existing entry covers a.m./p.m. and 24-hour time.

outcomes.statement: Use seconds as a unit, compare race times and choose seconds or minutes for an activity.

proposed.name: Convert between hours, minutes and seconds
proposed.why: MATH.measurement.unit-conversions is for metric units; time units are non-decimal and have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Convert between hours, minutes and seconds and add time durations.

proposed.name: Convert between hours, minutes and seconds
proposed.why: MATH.measurement.unit-conversions is for metric units; time units are non-decimal and have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Find the factors of a number using arrays and recognise numbers with only two factors as prime.
Find common multiples of two numbers using jumps on a number line.
Find common factors of two numbers.
Solve problems about events that repeat together using common multiples.
Sort numbers by divisibility by 2, 5 and 10.
Judge statements about factors, multiples, odd/even numbers and zero as true or false.
Describe locations and movements using directions (north, south, east, west) and landmarks.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Read a map to find routes and estimate distances.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

outcomes.statement: Draw a simple map or route plan of a familiar place.

proposed.name: Locate positions and describe routes using grids, maps and directions
proposed.why: MATH.geometry.positions covers relative position words only; grid locations, step-counted paths, map reading and compass directions have no entry.

sections.title: Food Wastage in the School Canteen

outcomes.statement: Collect survey data and organise it in a table of counts.
Read and draw pictographs where one symbol stands for several items.
Read and draw bar graphs, compare bars, find totals and make predictions.
Check whether statements about a picture or graph are true by counting and comparing.
